penetration_assumption: Base rate, VERIFIED: the whole dry-fruit category generates 5,971 bills / 12m = ~498 dry-fruit purchases a month across ~4,700 residents, i.e. roughly 1 in 10 residents buys a dry-fruit item in a month. Every new line is sized as a share of THOSE 498 monthly shoppers, never as a share of the population. Line-by-line, in plain words: (1) Protein bars Rs 65,000/yr — the one bar SKU ARY has ever stocked (Rite Bite Max Protein 50g) sold its entire 24-unit buy in 16 days across 20 bills at Rs 80, so ~1.5 bars/day; I assume a 4-SKU range settles at ~2x that single-SKU rate but the novelty rate halves, i.e. ~68 bars/month (range Rs 43,000-1,00,000 — this is one 16-day observation). (2) Chilgoza Rs 28,000 — 40 packs of 100g at Rs 700 over the Oct-Jan season only; ARY's highest-ticket working nut (Jivo Pista 250g at Rs 350) moves 185 units/yr, and chilgoza is 2x that ticket. (3) Kesar Rs 24,000 — 80 one-gram boxes/yr at Rs 300, a festival/kheer/prasad purchase. (4) Prunes + cranberry Rs 22,000 — Dry Apricot 250g is the proven health-driven dried-fruit shopper at 166 bills/yr; I assume each new SKU reaches 35% of that count at Rs 190. (5) Medjool dates Rs 18,000 — Loin Arbian Dates 500g did Rs 14,238 in the 4 months it was in stock. (6) Badam powder Rs 15,000 and (7) chironji Rs 12,000 — ~100-125 packs/yr each, no ARY analogue, weakest numbers here. (8) Jivo seeds restock Rs 68,500 — NOT an assumption: the line's own VERIFIED run-rate of Rs 5,709/month over the 7 months it was in stock, annualised. (9) Gud Chana Rs 27,000 and (10) Magaj Rs 9,500 — their own verified 12m sales, restored. (11) Panjeeri Rs 12,000 — assumed, no sales history.
probe_evidence: Ran `ary assort probe` (and hand-written SQL over ProductMaster x SaleDetail x SaleHeader x Stock x PurchaseDetail, window 2025-09-01 to 2026-08-31) on ~35 term sets with spelling variants. The supplied coverage diff is unreliable IN BOTH DIRECTIONS and I did not use its verdicts. FALSE COVERED it produced: "Dried prunes" matched on 'aloo' (potato), "Chironji" on 'foods', "Protein bars Rs 4.6 L" on 'pro', "Gajak Rs 1.19 L" on 'deep', "Chilgoza Rs 1.6 L" on 'nuts', "Nut cookies" on 'coffee', "Almonds Rs 4.03 L" on 'badam' — which is mostly Bajaj Almond Drops hair oil and Cadbury almond chocolate; real almond-as-food sales are Rs 3.60 L. TWO OF MY OWN "ABSENT" CALLS WERE WRONG AND I CAUGHT THEM ON A SECOND PASS: (i) gajak/revdi is spelled "Gazzak" at ARY and filed under General Items — 10 SKUs, Rs 90,480 in 12m (Mahalakshmi Gazzak 200g alone Rs 24,660 / 479 bills), all bought once on 2025-12-07..26 and sold out by Feb; (ii) char magaz is "Magaj 100 Gm" in Spices, Rs 9,500 / 91 bills; (iii) roasted chana is covered by Sunil Roasted Hing Chana 200g at Rs 71,640 / 1,286 bills. CONFIRMED ABSENT after 3-5 spelling variants each, zero rows across all 21,479 SKUs: chilgoza/pine nut/neoza; chironji/charoli/chiraunji/chirongi; saffron/kesar/zafran as a spice (all 'kesar' hits are flavoured milk and ice cream); prunes/aloo bukhara/bukhara/karonda; dried cranberry and dried blueberry as fruit (only juice and candy); Medjool/Ajwa/Mabroom/Sukkari/Kimia/Safawi; hazelnut/macadamia/pecan/Brazil as nuts (only chocolate); badam/dry-fruit powder; panchmeva/panjiri (2 Haldiram SKUs listed, never sold); protein/energy/date bars (1 SKU, Rs 1,920). THE DECIDING NUMBERS, all VERIFIED: Dry Fruits group (ProductGroupID=121) = 131 active SKUs, 51 sold in 12m, 80 dead, Rs 14,90,669 = 1.94% of ARY's Rs 7.67 Cr / 372,301 bills. 112 of 131 SKUs (85%) have zero on-hand TODAY, and 32 of the 51 that actually sell are at zero stock, carrying Rs 4,10,832 = 27.6% of the category's proven demand. 43 interior stockout months (a SKU sold before and after but not during) worth Rs 1,33,398. The entire Jivo seeds sub-line (chia, flax, pumpkin, sunflower, basil) sold every month Sep-25 to Mar-26 then went to EXACTLY zero on all five SKUs simultaneously, with zero stock and no purchase order since 2026-03-31. 13 almond brands are listed; 3 sell. MARGIN is derived from the purchase ledger, not a blanket rate: 40 SKUs with both a purchase and a sale in the window give a category gross margin of 12.67% (Rs 1,76,350 on Rs 13,91,872 net) — Raja Badam 8.0%, Raja Cashew 11.5%, while the gap lines are better: Jivo seeds 20-33%, makhana 17-19%, Magaj 17.2%, Gud Chana 16.3%, the Rite Bite bar 19.1%. Three Jivo gift boxes and Mix Nuts 250g sell AT OR BELOW cost (0%, -12.6%, -25.3%, -2.5%).
kill_reason: Not a kill — but the assortment gap is small and is NOT this category's problem, so it must not be presented as one. Rs 3.01 lakh of gap revenue (0.39% of ARY's Rs 7.67 Cr, Rs 56,846 of gross profit) sits against Rs 4,10,832 of ALREADY-PROVEN demand that is on an empty shelf today — 32 of the 51 dry-fruit SKUs that sell are at zero on-hand, 112 of 131 active SKUs have no stock at all, and 80 have not sold in 12 months. Adding SKUs here competes for the same working capital that is not refilling the ones that work. The one honest read: 56 of the 57 researched must-have lines have a working ARY equivalent; the 11 genuinely absent lines are all nice-to-have or should-have specialty items. The correct first action is a buying-cadence fix, not a range extension — restore the Jivo seeds PO (dead since 2026-03-31), put Gud Chana and Magaj back on the shelf, and place the Dec gazzak/rewari buy TWICE instead of once (that Rs 90,480 line sold out mid-season on a single December purchase). The only new line with a hard sell-through signal behind it is the protein bar: one SKU, 24 units, gone in 16 days, never reordered.

Dried prunes 200g — zero SKUs across 5 spellings; Dry Apricot 250g (Rs 28,415 / 166 bills) proves the health-driven dried-fruit shopper exists
Dried cranberry 200g — zero SKUs as fruit; only cranberry juice is listed
Premium dates Medjool / Ajwa 250g — zero named-variety SKUs; Loin Arbian Dates 500g did Rs 14,238 in the 4 months it was stocked
Badam / dry-fruit powder 200g — zero SKUs; the baby and elderly cohort, and the grind-on-demand service the research flags
Chironji / charoli 50g — zero SKUs across 4 spellings; small recipe and prasad item
RESTOCK (already listed, zero stock, no PO since 2026-03-31): Jivo Chia / Flax / Pumpkin / Sunflower / Basil Seeds 200g — Rs 5,709/month run-rate, five SKUs went dark in the same month
RESTOCK: Luxmi Gud Chana 160g — Rs 26,880 on 524 bills last winter, zero stock since March, bought once on 2026-01-14
RESTOCK: Magaj 100g (char magaz) — Rs 9,500 on 91 bills, zero stock since May
STOCK FOR THE FIRST TIME: Haldiram Panjeeri Ladoo 800g / Burfi 400g — listed, never sold, prasad-adjacent on this campus

DELIST, do not stock: the 80 dead Dry Fruits SKUs — 13 almond brands are listed and 3 sell (King, Star, Paras, Pari, Tulip, Krishna, Jawahar, Vinit, Gauri, Bright Star, Aman, Tata Sampann all at zero); they split existing demand rather than adding any

DO NOT ADD: exotic nuts (hazelnut, pecan, macadamia, Brazil) and premium dried berries — every premium-brand 250g SKU already on ARY's list is dead (Tata Sampann x5, Bite N Bites x2, Kirkland Trail Mix, Food Studio, Nut Star, Brill, Silvernut all Rs 0)
blockers: CAPITAL COMPETES WITH ITSELF — 32 of the 51 selling dry-fruit SKUs are at zero on-hand right now, carrying Rs 4,10,832 of proven 12m demand. Any rupee spent on the 11 new lines is a rupee not spent refilling those. The gap buy should be funded from the 80 dead SKUs' shelf, not from new working capital.

THIN CATEGORY MARGIN, VERIFIED FROM THE PURCHASE LEDGER — 12.67% blended (Raja Badam 8.0%, Raja Cashew 11.5%). Rs 3.01 lakh of new revenue only carries Rs 56,846 of gross profit. The research's own margin lever — buying bulk and repacking into ARY's own 250g/500g pouches (8-18% becomes 25-40%) — needs an FSSAI licence for the repacking activity plus Legal Metrology declarations, which are not on record for ARY. Until that exists the category cannot escape the branded-pack margin.

SUPPLIER REACH FROM RAJGARH — chilgoza is a Kinnaur/Reckong Peo crop ~350 km away and ARY has no vendor for it; Medjool/Ajwa dates and dried prunes/cranberry are importer lines that the Nahan/Solan distributors ARY buys from (Raja, Sunil, King, Mahalakshmi) do not carry. Each of the four specialty lines needs a new supplier, not a bigger order to an existing one.

ORDERING CADENCE IS THE ROOT CAUSE, AND IT IS NOT A MONEY PROBLEM — the Jivo seeds line has had no purchase order since 2026-03-31 despite five SKUs selling every month before that; Gud Chana was bought once (2026-01-14) and Magaj once (2026-05-13). The Rs 90,480 gazzak/rewari winter line was bought on 2025-12-07..26 ONLY and every one of its 10 SKUs was sold out by mid-February with sales still live. A single missed December buy costs that whole season.

PACK ARCHITECTURE — only 3 of 131 SKUs are sold by weight (Khajoor, two Coconut Gari); everything else is a pre-packed 250g piece at a Rs 230-380 ticket against ARY's Rs 205.65 average bill. There is no weigh-and-pack counter, so a resident who wants 100g of badam cannot buy it. Anjeer is the tell: the 100g pack sells Rs 52,260 on 258 bills while the 250g pack has never sold.

SHELF AND PEST — dry-fruit moth and beetle in a humid monsoon; the 250g sealed pre-pack limits this today, but any move to loose bulk (the margin lever) brings FIFO, airtight bins and monthly inspection with it.

DISTRIBUTION, NOT ASSORTMENT — dry fruits are sold at Ary Pos only (Rs 14.55 L) plus Rs 35,640 at Ary Clothing. Nothing at Ary G Canteen, Girls Canteen Ts or Ary Lite, which together take 81,815 bills a year. The impulse formats that would sell there (single-serve nut packs, flavoured makhana, bars) are listed and dead. Fixing the counter placement costs nothing.

NOT CHECKED — whether the langar/hostel kitchens buy dry fruit elsewhere. Identified institutional dry-fruit purchases total only ~Rs 86,000 (Akal Academy Rs 34,114, Kalgidhar Trust Rs 20,818, De-Addiction Ward Rs 11,014, Mess Rs 5,849) = 5.8% of the category, and 97% of ARY's bills carry no identified buyer. The bulk-indent adjacency the research proposes cannot be sized from this database; it needs a human to ask the langar store.

NO COLD CHAIN OR LICENCE BLOCKER for the lines as scoped — every item here is ambient and needs no FSSAI beyond ARY's existing retail registration, as long as ARY sells sealed manufacturer packs and does not repack.
